unassigned_nodes.reason: Tzedakah (charity/righteousness) is inherently a holy mitzvah — a positive spiritual act. The only existing package is evil (הִרְהוּרֵי נִאוּף וְאֲבִי אָבוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה). Assigning צדקה there would be assigning by causal connection (it combats those thoughts) rather than by essential nature. Tzedakah's essential nature is holiness and giving, the opposite of impurity and death. No good package exists in this Torah to receive it.

unassigned_nodes.reason: This is a halakhic/ethical directive from Pirkei Avot about guarding oneself — a protective boundary rooted in holiness. Its essential nature is positive guidance (mussar/halacha), not impurity. It cannot be placed in the evil package, and no good package exists in this Torah.

This node describes the positive effect of charity — 'very effective for being saved from lecherous thoughts.' Its essential nature is salvation and rescue (הצלה), a good spiritual outcome. Although it references lecherous thoughts, the node itself is about being saved from them, which is a holy result. It does not belong in the evil package by essential nature.
